summary: Verified Register.jsx name-field expansion (First/Second name + First/Second last name) across all three registration flows (Create-account for OHIP+Private, Re-establish Care, and New-patient). Frontend joinName() correctly combines and trims. Backend contract is unchanged and persists the combined values verbatim. All 6 pytest tests passed; all UI flows pass; payloads inspected on wire confirm combined first_name / last_name values.
critical_code_review_comments: Register.jsx submit() for OHIP/Private/Tourist uses joinName() but also spreads the entire form (including now-unused second_name/second_last_name) into the register payload. Backend RegisterBody currently ignores unknown fields, but for cleanliness those two extras should be stripped before POST to avoid silent schema drift.
submitNewPatient() re-implements the join inline (map+trim+filter+join) instead of reusing joinName(); duplicated logic — extract to a single helper.

Backend still calls `.strip()` on the incoming first_name/last_name in /auth/register, /applications/return-request, and /applications/new-patient, but does NOT collapse interior double spaces. Frontend does; anyone hitting the API directly could store 'Juan  Carlos'. Consider normalising server-side (`re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip()`).
